saints.name: St. Joseph
saints.title: Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary
saints.shortBlurb: The just man of Nazareth, guardian of the Redeemer and husband of Our Lady, patron of the universal Church…
biography: Joseph, a carpenter of Nazareth of the house of David, was espoused to Mary. Warned by an angel in a dream, he took her as his wife though she was found with child; again in dreams he was bidden to flee with the Child into Egypt from Herod, and to return after Herod's death.

Scripture records no word of his, only his ready obedience, and calls him a just man. He appears last in the Gospel at the finding of the twelve-year-old Jesus in the Temple, and tradition holds that he died before the Lord's public ministry, in the presence of Jesus and Mary.

Long venerated as guardian of the Redeemer, he was declared Patron of the Universal Church by Pius IX on 8 December 1870, and Pius XII in 1955 set his feast as model of workers on the first of May. Patron of workers and of fathers, he is invoked above all for a happy death, having died, as devotion holds, in the arms of Jesus and Mary.
saints.knownFor: Guarding the Holy Family in faithful, silent obedience.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; Patron of the Universal Church (1870)

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 19 March
